name: Scraping Bee

modes.label: Browser API request (not time-priced)
modes.note: Headless browser accessed as a request/JS-scenario API. JS rendering is ON by default, so a default request costs 5 credits, not 1. Each request is capped at 140 s. Only successful 200/404/410 (and, per the rendered docs, 413) responses are billed. Effective price per 1,000 default JS requests ranges from $1.27 (Hobby: $19/75k credits) to $0.37 (Business+: $599/8M credits). No browser-hour price.

plans.name: Hobby
plans.note: 75,000 API credits/month; VAT excluded. JS rendering, rotating+premium proxies, geotargeting, screenshots/extraction/Google API and dedicated scraper APIs are included. NO priority email support, dedicated account manager or team management (Business and Business+ only). Credits expire at the end of the billing cycle (no rollover).

plans.name: Freelance
plans.note: 250,000 API credits/month; VAT excluded. No priority support, account manager or team management. Credits don't roll over.

plans.name: Startup
plans.note: 1,000,000 API credits/month; VAT excluded. No priority support, account manager or team management. Credits don't roll over.

plans.name: Business
plans.note: 3,000,000 API credits/month; VAT excluded; paid features shared.

plans.name: Business+
plans.note: 8,000,000 API credits/month; VAT excluded; paid features shared.

plans.name: Custom
plans.note: More credits or concurrency by quote.

features.ip_note: Default classic rotating proxies (type unstated); premium_proxy=residential (25 credits with JS) and stealth_proxy pool (75 credits), both geotargetable; own_proxy BYO; billed per request, no per-GB price.

caveats: Storage, snapshot GiB-month and public IPv4 prices are not published in the reviewed sources; null is not free.

No guaranteed vCPU allocation published; browser-hour is not a verified 4-vCPU/8-GiB VM equivalent. The sizes card keeps unknown hardware null; do not coerce it to zero or auto-rank against resource-guaranteed VMs.
Browser RAM is not published unless a specific mode overrides it.
Request API is adjacent to long-lived agent browsers. JS scenarios/screenshots do not establish an eight-hour persistent CDP session product. Browser-hour and 4/8 normalized prices remain null.
Proxy consumption is packaged into request credits; do not also invent a GB fee. Browser profiles, recording storage and independent GPU/OS tiers are not published.
Credit allowance divided by fee is not a guaranteed overage rate. Auto-mode can select more expensive request configurations; cap via max_cost parameter.
FAQ on running out: 'Either upgrade your plan for the current month ... Or you can early renew your current subscription in two clicks.' There is no per-credit overage rate.
Stealth proxy without JS is 'coming soon'. Only stealth+JS (75 credits) is live.
Usage API (credits and concurrency readout) is rate-limited to 6 calls/min. Exceeding plan concurrency returns 429 (not billed): 'Please upgrade your plan or contact sales.'

Credits expire every billing cycle (no rollover). The cycle ends EARLY when credits run out, and the subscription then auto-renews. Running out therefore means paying the next full plan fee early, i.e. overage is billed in whole-plan chunks, or you upgrade. Without renewal or upgrade, requests fail with 401.

fleet.verification: Trial: no card needed. A payment method is required for any subscription.
fleet.tiers: Paid Hobby 25, Freelance 50, Startup 100, Business 200, Business+ 400; higher by product expert.
fleet.notes: Free 1,000-credit trial has no numeric simultaneous-request quota verified here, so default null rather than 25 paid slots. 10 fits Hobby, 50 Freelance, 300 Business+, 1,000 custom. Requests not retained VMs.

audit_2026_09_29.source: checked against the provider's live pricing and docs pages

snapshot_auto.note: N/A by design: stateless per-request scraping API (GET/POST/PUT https://app.scrapingbee.com/api/v1/ with a url). There is no user machine or persistent browser session. The only continuity is session_id, which keeps the same proxy IP for 5 minutes, plus cookies you pass per request.

snapshot_on_demand.quote: Fetch arbitrary URLs through ScrapingBee, with JavaScript rendering, proxy controls, browser interactions, screenshots, downloads, and data extraction.
snapshot_on_demand.note: No machine/session to snapshot; screenshots are page images, not state checkpoints.

harness_api.quote: Ask a GPT model through ScrapingBee, optionally with web-enhanced search.
harness_api.note: AI features are one-shot prompt->answer endpoints (ChatGPT/Gemini APIs, ai_query/ai_extract_rules extraction). Remote MCP and LangChain expose ScrapingBee as tools to external agents. No agent harness runs inside a ScrapingBee sandbox.

ingress_rules.note: Customers never get a machine or exposed port; the only inbound surface is ScrapingBee's own API endpoint (auth via Bearer API key) and the Remote MCP endpoint (API key in URL). There is nothing customer-side to apply ingress/allowlist rules to, so provider-side control over 'who reaches exposed ports' does not apply to this product.

guest_firewall.note: No shell or machine access. Only js_scenario/evaluate page JavaScript runs in ScrapingBee's headless browser.

volume_attach.quote: Non-HTML downloads are limited to 2 MB per request.
volume_attach.note: No storage product. Outputs are returned in the HTTP response; the CLI writes exports locally.

volume_shared.quote: Fetch arbitrary URLs through ScrapingBee, with JavaScript rendering, proxy controls, browser interactions, screenshots, downloads, and data extraction.
volume_shared.note: ScrapingBee is a stateless request/response scraping API (single endpoint https://app.scrapingbee.com/api/v1/, no persistent machine). There is no volume/disk product at all, so a volume mounted by several machines at once is plainly outside the product; docs and pricing page never mention storage or volumes.

image_oci.quote: Fetch arbitrary URLs through ScrapingBee, with JavaScript rendering, proxy controls, browser interactions, screenshots, downloads, and data extraction.
image_oci.note: not offered: outside the product's scope (stateless scraping API, no customer machine/image to boot)

computer_use.quote: Click, scroll and type before scraping
computer_use.note: The JavaScript Scenario feature drives page interactions via a declarative instruction list (click/scroll/type/wait), not a screenshot+click computer-use API against a visible desktop.

captcha_solving.quote: Basic visual CAPTCHA challenges could be solved with software like OCR ... Services like 2Captcha and Death by Captcha use real people to solve CAPTCHAs for a fee.
captcha_solving.note: ScrapingBee's own guidance points users to third-party CAPTCHA-solving services rather than describing a built-in solver; ScrapingBee's stealth/premium proxies aim to avoid triggering CAPTCHAs, not solve them.

soc2.quote: ScrapingBee may satisfy this obligation by providing an up-to-date SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, or equivalent third-party assurance report
soc2.note: DPA states ScrapingBee can satisfy customer audit rights via its own SOC 2 Type II report.

hipaa.quote: ScrapingBee may satisfy this obligation by providing an up-to-date SOC 2 Type II report, ISO 27001 certificate, or equivalent third-party assurance report
hipaa.note: No mention of HIPAA eligibility or a BAA anywhere in the DPA, privacy policy, or GDPR notice.

sso.note: Business plans mention team management but no SAML/OIDC single sign-on is documented on pricing, docs, or legal pages.

static_egress_ip.note: The only IP-continuity feature documented is session_id, which pins the same rotating/premium/stealth proxy IP for 5 minutes per session, not a fixed dedicated outbound IP. own_proxy lets the customer BYO a proxy, but ScrapingBee itself does not offer a static egress IP; no page advertises one.

eu_data_residency.quote: Processing Locations Primarily – EU. All cross-border transfers are governed by EU SCCs as set out in Exhibit 2.
eu_data_residency.note: DPA Exhibit 1 states processing locations are primarily EU, and Exhibit 2 lists the main infrastructure sub-processors (Google Cloud Platform - Paris main with EU multi-DC backup; Datapacket - Netherlands/France/Czech Republic) as EU-based with no transfer mechanism required (EEA). There is no customer-selectable region picker, but the provider's own infrastructure keeps data in the EU by default.
